Reporting to the Water Resources Manager, the Hydrogeologist is responsible for providing technical expertise and support related to groundwater and surface water management for NewRange Copper Nickel’s mining projects. The Hydrogeologist contributes to the development of water management strategies, supports hydrogeologic modeling and analysis, and ensures that water-related risks, costs, and operational requirements are clearly understood and integrated into project planning and decision-making.

Support development and application of hydrogeologic and hydrologic models to evaluate site conditions and project scenarios.

Contribute to planning and design analyses, providing recommendations related to dewatering, water management, and closure strategies.

Support development of site-wide water management plans, including water balance, handling, storage, and reuse strategies.
Collaborate with mine engineering, geology, geotechnical, environmental, permitting and operations teams to integrate water management into project design.

Support identification of risks and opportunities related to water management, including cost, schedule, and operational impacts.

Experience in preparing and reviewing technical reports and studies for internal and external stakeholders.
Professional designation in Minnesota State (e.g., P.G. or P.E.), or ability to acquire is considered an asset.

Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present technical information clearly.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to work collaboratively across technical teams and stakeholders.
Proficiency with hydrogeologic modeling tools and Microsoft Office Suite.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic project environment.
